notes.house: mu = 0.42 + 0.92*lean + 4.5*inc + E, prior sd 7.4 (lean = 0.75 x (2024 president - nation) + 0.25 x (2020 president - nation) on the 2026 maps, margin points, from precinct returns; fitted on the contested seats of 2018 and 2022 with the same lean on those maps, the intercept = the fitted year intercepts minus those years' national House vote), fundraising: + 1.31 x log(D / R individual contributions through June 30, $10k floor) - out of sample it cut competitive-seat error 5.5 % (2018) and 3.8 % (2022), and moves incumbency from 4.5 to 3.3; race polls from the state pages blended by precision (per-poll sd 5.6, shared 4.3, Student-t with 10 degrees of freedom; a poll's precision fades with a 63-day half-life, no hard window); seats with no Democrat or no Republican on the ballot are decided (CA-40 R-v-R, D-v-D top-two), an independent incumbent facing only a Democrat (CA-6) keeps incumbency; every race poll (House and Senate) is corrected for its pollster's measured lean (538's 2016-22 record, shrunk) or, failing that, its sponsor tag: D-sponsored polls ran 4.3 too Democratic and R-sponsored 4.1 too Republican against the non-partisan polls of the same race (1998-2022, same sign every cycle), and count at 0.58 weight; polls with more than 12 % undecided carry up to 26 % more error, a third candidate at 10 %+ 27 % more; LV and RV race polls are not adjusted (94 % of late race polls are LV; the generic-ballot fit carries LV/RV/adult offsets); Hispanic/Asian swing since 2024: + 12 x centred Hispanic CVAP share (Cubans at 0.25) + 11 x centred Asian share, before the poll blend (2025 NJ/VA governor and CA Prop 50 reversed the 2020-24 shift fully, specials did not; centred so the national environment is unchanged); no race poll is shifted for the direction its state's polls missed before; the demographic factors are updated from the district polls (Bayesian, no tuned parameters: 2022 House log loss -5.1 %) - today the polls put the Hispanic factor at -10 per unit share against the +12 prior swing and white non-college at +5.8; regional Hispanic deviations (prior zero, set by the district polls): Texas +4.5, Florida -1.1, West -4.3; heating-oil adjustment (judgment, not backtested): fuel-oil household share x the year's change in retail heating oil (EIA weekly Maine residential price $6.03 for the week of 2026-10-19, v $3.23 a year earlier) x 650 gal x 1.04 pts per $1,000 x the share not yet in the race's polls (the change since its newest poll in full, the change before that at 50 %; a race with no polls 50 %), in either direction, against the president's party (Maine Senate +0.41); national environment E = our generic-ballot trend, with no correction for the direction of a polling miss; national-vote error 3.9 at 9 days out (the root-mean-square miss of the generic-ballot average against the House vote at this distance, 15 cycles 1996-2024, in either direction); errors t5: national 4.4 (the vote error plus the year-to-year error of the contested-seat intercept, 2), state 2.5, urban 2, Hispanic / Cuban / Asian group factors 15 per unit share, residual 5
notes.senate: mu = 0.7 + 0.80*E + 0.84*lean + 6.7*inc, prior sd 8.79 (D-v-R races 1982-2024 with time-trending lean and incumbency slopes, evaluated at 2026), polls from the Wikipedia race pages (per-poll sd 4.2; race-level systematic 3.3 = the measured midterm total 4 minus the shared statewide shock drawn separately); only polls of the candidates actually on the ballot, full field where a third candidate polls 10 %+; the margin is the main challenger minus the Republican - an independent where no Democrat is on the ballot (NE, ID, SD) or the independent leads the Democrat (MT). Independent wins are not counted as Democratic seats. With no Democrat on the ballot an independent's prior sd is sqrt(8.79^2 + 9^2) = 12.6, and a funded one (>= 25 % of the Republican's June 30 money) starts 12 points better than a Democrat would: the four such races since 1988 (Orman 2014, McMullin 2022, Osborn 2024, Walker for Alaska governor 2014) beat the D-v-R prior by 21-33 points (mean +26), the four with no money ran -1 to -49 (Harrington 2020, O'Hara 2002, Spannaus 1990, Steve Osborn 2006); no dollar floor (Orman had $0.63M), and the record places the cut only between no money and Orman's 0.45x; the full +26 scored worse than +12 2-4 weeks out on those races, whose late polls ran ahead of the results. With a Democrat also running (MT) the D-v-R prior is kept, widened x2 (independents who outpolled the Democrat finished 2 points from it on average, sd 13); Hispanic/Asian swing term as in the House (12 x centred Hispanic CVAP share, Cubans at 0.25, 11 x Asian; state shares vs national), mean and group shocks both damped by the Senate's national slope 0.795; no correction for the direction of a state's polling miss; heating-oil adjustment by state fuel-oil share; appointed incumbents (Husted, Moody) get 0.6 of the incumbency term (12 appointees 2006-22 averaged +6.3 over an open-seat prior); the simulation draws a shared statewide polling miss of 3.1 pts in either direction (the root-mean-square of the cycle-wide statewide miss 1998-2022) plus 2.83 pts of extra race-level spread, on top of the 3.3 the blend keeps - together more than the measured race-average miss; the split was tuned on the walk-forward backtest, where it scored seat counts better calibrated and the correlation between races closer to the 0.13 past cycles show (governors keep 4.2 with no extra); the prior's lean and incumbency slopes follow their 1982-2024 trends (incumbency worth less, lean more, a tighter prior than a pooled fit), drawn with correlation 0.3 to the House's national draw (the generic-ballot miss and the Senate's shared polling miss correlated about +0.3 over 13 cycles, not 1)
notes.backtests: House, each year forecast from the other years' data: on 15 Sep the model gave Democrats 227 seats (202-257) in 2018 against 235 won, PIT 0.69, and 213 (191-234) in 2022 against 213, PIT 0.49. Over 12 dates from July to November the result fell inside the 10-90 % range every time, and the model ran Republican at most dates (mean PIT 0.65). Senate, 2018-2024 at 6 dates each: the seat count fell inside the 10-90 % range at all 24, and the races ran the other way, too Democratic at most dates (mean PIT 0.29): in all four cycles the Senate polls missed toward the Republicans, a direction this model deliberately does not assume.
